subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In Roman Catholic teaching, marriage is understood to be...
options: A civil agreement that can be dissolved at will
A purely private matter with no religious meaning
questions.explain: Catholics regard marriage as one of the seven sacraments, a sacred and lifelong union blessed by God.

questions.q: According to the Gospels, who taught 'What God has joined together, let no one separate'?
questions.explain: Jesus spoke these words (Mark 10:9), which are used to support the belief that marriage should be lifelong.

questions.q: Which papal encyclical teaches that Catholics should not use artificial contraception?
questions.explain: Humanae Vitae (1968) reaffirmed Catholic opposition to artificial methods of contraception.

questions.q: Which pope issued the 1968 encyclical Humanae Vitae?
questions.explain: Pope Paul VI issued Humanae Vitae in 1968, upholding the ban on artificial contraception.

questions.q: Which New Testament verse is often used to support gender equality, stating there is 'neither male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus'?
questions.explain: Paul's words in Galatians 3:28 are used to argue that men and women are equal before God.

questions.q: What is the term for a family made up of two parents and their children living together?
questions.explain: A nuclear family consists of two parents and their dependent children in one household.

questions.q: What is the term for the choice to abstain from marriage and sexual relationships, as taken by Catholic priests and nuns?
questions.explain: Celibacy is the choice to remain unmarried and abstain from sexual relationships, often for religious reasons.

questions.q: The teaching 'male and female he created them' (Genesis 1:27) is often understood by Christians to mean...
options: Men and women are equal in value and both made in God's image
Men are naturally superior to women
Women should never work outside the home
Only men truly reflect God's image
questions.explain: Genesis 1:27 is used to teach that both sexes share equal dignity as beings made in the image of God.

questions.q: Why do many Christians believe marriage should last for life?
options: Because the couple make sacred vows before God that should not be broken
Because it is cheaper than divorcing
Because marriage carries no religious meaning
questions.explain: Christian marriage vows are seen as a lifelong, sacred commitment made in the presence of God.

questions.q: Why does the Catholic Church traditionally oppose artificial contraception?
options: Because sexual intercourse should remain open to the possibility of creating new life
Because it believes sex is always sinful
Because it wants families to be smaller
questions.explain: Catholic teaching holds that sex should keep both its unitive and procreative purposes, so artificial contraception is rejected.

questions.q: Some Christians hold a 'complementarian' view of gender. This means they believe...
options: Men and women are equal but have different, complementary roles
Men and women should have completely identical roles
Gender is unimportant within the family
questions.explain: A complementarian view holds that the sexes are of equal worth but suited to different roles that complete one another.

questions.q: The biblical command to 'be fruitful and multiply' is used by many Christians to teach that a purpose of marriage is...
questions.explain: The command in Genesis is used to support procreation as a key purpose of Christian marriage.

questions.q: Why do many Protestant Christians accept the use of contraception?
options: They believe it allows responsible family planning and does not destroy a life already conceived
They believe sex has no purpose
questions.explain: Many Protestant churches permit contraception as a responsible way to plan a family, distinguishing it from abortion.

questions.q: Why do many Christians disapprove of cohabitation (living together before marriage)?
options: Because they believe sexual relationships should take place only within marriage
Because it is against the law
Because it prevents a couple from having children
questions.explain: Many Christians teach that sex belongs within the lifelong commitment of marriage, so they discourage cohabitation.

questions.q: A married Catholic couple wish to space out having children without disobeying Church teaching. Which method would the Catholic Church permit?
questions.explain: The Catholic Church permits natural family planning because it does not use artificial means to prevent conception.

questions.q: A Catholic whose marriage has broken down wishes to remarry in the Church. Which process might allow this by declaring the first marriage was never valid?
questions.explain: The Catholic Church does not recognise divorce but may grant an annulment if the marriage is found never to have been valid.

questions.q: A woman wishes to become an ordained priest. Which of the following is true?
options: The Church of England ordains women as priests, but the Roman Catholic Church does not
Both Churches ordain women as priests
Only the Roman Catholic Church ordains women
questions.explain: The Church of England has ordained women priests since 1994, whereas the Roman Catholic Church restricts priestly ordination to men.

questions.q: A married person begins a sexual relationship with someone who is not their husband or wife. Which of the Ten Commandments does this break?
questions.explain: Adultery is sexual unfaithfulness within marriage and breaks the commandment 'You shall not commit adultery'.

specSource: Eduqas GCSE Religious Studies specification; Component 3: Issues of Relationships
